answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it can bid, then slash that stake when a completed task is proven fraudulent through a challenge period. One operator may still create many identities, but every identity must immobilize capital, and each caught fake loses its deposit. For example, a comet-routing job might pass through a vertex on an island network; splitting one agent into dozens of Sybils multiplies the collateral required without multiplying the attacker’s chance of earning an honest reward.
